short_definition: Consumers aged 50 and above who form a fast-growing, financially powerful, and digitally active market segment.
long_explanation: Silver Spenders (also called the Silver Generation) are consumers 50 and older who hold a large share of household wealth and drive a growing share of global consumer spending, especially in fashion, luxury, retail, technology, and finance. They matter to marketers because they are discretionary and quality-focused spenders rather than purely need-based buyers, they show strong brand loyalty once earned, and they are increasingly active online, reviewing products and engaging with brands digitally. To reach them, brands need to move from age-based to lifestyle-based segmentation.
usage_context: Boston Consulting Group data shows consumers aged 50-70 account for nearly 27% of spending across key categories (about $7 trillion annually), and McKinsey data projecting the Silver Generation will drive 48% of global spending growth in fashion, luxury, and beauty by 2025.
related_terms: Silver Economy, Gümüş Nesil, stage not age segmentation, omnichannel strategy, granfluencer, age-positive marketing
tr_definition: 50 yaş ve üzeri, hızla büyüyen, finansal açıdan güçlü ve dijitalde aktif bir tüketici segmentidir.
notes: The English and Turkish sections are not exact translations of each other; the Turkish section contains additional statistics (e.g. Euromonitor 2040 projections, granfluencer discussion) not present in the English section. Both were used to build this entry.

short_definition: A multi-skilled marketer who uses AI to unify strategy, content, media planning, and analytics into one workflow.
long_explanation: The Supermarketer is a marketing role empowered by AI to orchestrate strategy, content creation, media planning, and analytics under a single workflow, increasing campaign speed and enabling more personalized, consistent customer experiences across channels. It matters for marketers because it breaks down organizational silos between creative and analytical functions, but it also carries risks such as low-quality AI-generated content, data ethics issues, and loss of human touch if not managed with clear quality standards.
usage_context: The term was discussed in the Decoding AI for Marketing podcast episode "Entering the Age of Supermarketers," featuring guest Sandeep Menon of Auxia. It builds on the AI Orchestrator concept.
related_terms: AI Orchestrator, Prompt Library, 1P data, zero-party data, ROI
tr_equivalent: Supermarketer (Türkçe blogda İngilizce terim aynen kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Yapay zeka desteğiyle strateji, içerik, medya planlama ve analitiği tek bir iş akışında birleştiren çok yetkinlikli pazarlamacı rolüdür.
notes: The file ends with leftover assistant/chat text not part of the blog content: a line offering to prepare LinkedIn posts and Reels prompts next, followed by the question "İlk olarak LinkedIn metinlerini mi hazırlamamı istersin?" This was excluded from the entry but is flagged here as instructed.

short_definition: The persuasive impact of AI-generated or AI-managed digital personas, virtual influencers, and algorithmically optimized content on consumer behavior.
long_explanation: Synthetic Influence describes how AI-generated personas, virtual influencers, and data-optimized messaging shape consumer decisions, amplified through aesthetic design, sentiment analysis, and algorithmic targeting rather than human authenticity alone. It matters for marketers because influencers no longer need to be human, brand impact can now be predicted and engineered through language models, and smaller brands can use AI to produce high-impact campaigns without the reach of large budgets. Transparency about what is AI-generated versus real is critical to maintaining consumer trust.
usage_context: Yaniv Makover, CEO of Anyword, speaking on the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast (Episode 21), who says LLMs can predict which diaper ad will perform better with parents, and names virtual influencers Lil Miquela and Imma as examples of synthetic personas with millions of followers.
related_terms: virtual influencers, LLM (Large Language Models), Anyword, brand ambassador, sentiment analysis, algorithmic targeting
tr_definition: Yapay zeka tarafından oluşturulan dijital kişiliklerin, sanal etkileyicilerin ve algoritmik olarak optimize edilmiş içeriklerin tüketici davranışları üzerindeki ikna edici etkisidir.

short_definition: The impatience, excitement, or anxiety people feel while waiting for a reply to a digital message.
long_explanation: Textpectation, a blend of "text" and "expectation," describes the emotional state created by instant-messaging cues like typing indicators and read receipts, where delayed replies trigger anxiety about being ignored. It matters for marketers because consumers now hold brands to the same instant-response standard they hold friends to, especially through chatbots and social media, and slow responses are read as a sign of brand indifference. Managing this expectation is both a risk and an opportunity for building consumer trust and emotional connection.
related_terms: CRM, chatbot, digital anxiety, response time, brand reliability, personalization
tr_equivalent: Textpectation (Türkçe blogda İngilizce terim aynen kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Dijital bir mesaja yanıt beklerken hissedilen sabırsızlık, heyecan ya da kaygı halidir.

short_definition: A consumer cohort defined not by age but by having its preferences and decisions actively guided by AI recommendation systems.
long_explanation: The Algorithm Generation refers to consumers whose content and brand choices are shaped in real time by algorithmic recommendation systems such as those on Netflix, TikTok, YouTube, and Spotify, rather than by traditional generational or cultural markers. It matters for marketers because this audience expects content to be curated specifically for them instantly, prefers curated discovery over active search, and responds better to timely micro-interactions than to broad brand messaging. Marketing has to shift from static campaigns to adaptive, learning systems built on behavioral data.
usage_context: The term is attributed to Jocelyn Goldfein, former Director of Engineering at Facebook, speaking on Episode 17 of the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast (hosted by Greg Stuart, CEO of MMA Global, and Rex Briggs, Chief AI Officer at Claritas), quoting her: "The Algorithm Generation doesn't just consume content, they expect content to be curated specifically for them, in real time."
related_terms: behavioral maps, real-time personalization, micro-moments, anticipation-driven marketing, Decoding AI for Marketers podcast
tr_equivalent: Algoritma Kuşağı (blogda genellikle İngilizce "The Algorithm Generation" olarak kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Yaşla değil, algoritmik öneri sistemleri tarafından yönlendirilen tercih ve kararlarla tanımlanan bir tüketici kuşağıdır.

short_definition: The long-term business return, in loyalty, wallet share, and lifetime value, that comes from a brand deliberately building consumer trust.
long_explanation: The Trust Dividend describes the tangible payoff, increased customer loyalty, higher share of wallet, cross-selling opportunities, and higher customer lifetime value, that results from a brand consistently acting on authentic purpose and delivering trustworthy customer experiences. It reframes trust-building as a measurable business driver rather than a soft or optional value, although linking trust to financial outcomes remains a real measurement challenge for CFOs and marketers alike. It also ties responsible, transparent use of AI and customer data directly to whether that trust is gained or lost.
usage_context: Linda Boff, Global CMO of GE, described on the Building Better CMOs podcast (hosted by Greg Stuart) how GE's purpose of powering a third of the world and reaching billions of patients builds pride and trust. Other examples: Lisa Caputo of Travelers on the value of "care," Andy Rebhun of Cava on authenticity and consistency driving trust and trial, Ravi Kandikonda of Zillow on best products being the best brands, and the fact that T-Mobile's CMO spends 70% of their time on customer experience.
related_terms: customer experience (CX), multi-touch attribution (MTA), share of wallet, customer lifetime value (LTV), brand authenticity, Building Better CMOs podcast
tr_definition: Bir markanın bilinçli olarak güven inşa etmesi sonucunda elde ettiği sadakat, cüzdan payı ve müşteri yaşam boyu değeri artışı gibi uzun vadeli iş getirisidir.
notes: The English section explicitly states the term "Trust Dividend" is not itself used in the underlying podcast sources but was coined by the blog author to summarize the pattern; this should be checked by an editor since it affects how the term's origin is presented.

short_definition: A mobile-native, vertically scrolled digital comic format, originating in South Korea, published in short serialized episodes.
long_explanation: A Webtoon is a digital comic designed for vertical scrolling on mobile devices, delivered in short episodes (roughly 2-5 minutes to read) with interactive features like comments and likes. It matters for marketers because webtoons function as branded storytelling platforms and loyalty tools, offering character-driven campaign opportunities, transmedia extensions into games, music, and film, and a direct channel to reach Gen Z and Millennial audiences who show high loyalty and emotional investment in the format.
usage_context: Netflix's adaptation of the webtoon Chicken Nugget into a series as an example of webtoon IP crossing into other media, and names platforms Naver Webtoon, KakaoPage, Line Webtoon, Tapas, and Tappytoon as part of the format's global spread.
related_terms: branded content, transmedia marketing, Gen Z, Gen Alpha, IP (intellectual property), influencer partnerships
tr_equivalent: Webtoon (Türkçe blogda İngilizce terim aynen kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Güney Kore kökenli, mobil cihazlar için tasarlanmış, dikey kaydırmalı ve kısa bölümler halinde yayınlanan dijital çizgi roman formatıdır.

short_definition: An approach where AI capabilities are integrated into a single end-to-end workflow instead of being used as separate, manually connected point tools.
long_explanation: Workflow-First AI moves businesses away from using isolated AI tools for single tasks (like image recognition or translation) that require manual integration, toward unified systems that pass data and context automatically between stages of a process. It matters for marketers and other business functions because it reduces the time and error associated with manually stitching together point solutions, and enables contextual understanding and real-time adaptation across an entire process such as e-commerce, healthcare, finance, or manufacturing operations.
usage_context: Industry applications include full automation from customer experience to logistics in e-commerce, integrated patient management from diagnosis to treatment in healthcare, risk analysis to automated loan approval in finance, and production planning to quality control in manufacturing.
related_terms: point tools, contextual understanding, dynamic adaptation, integrated decision-making
tr_definition: Yapay zeka yeteneklerinin, elle birleştirilen ayrı araçlar yerine tek bir uçtan uca iş akışında entegre edildiği bir yaklaşımdır.
notes: The folder name "Workflow-First" was expanded to "Workflow-First AI" for the term field because that is the full name the blog itself uses throughout.

short_definition: AI-generated work output that looks polished and professional but is incomplete, irrelevant, or lacks real value, and creates hidden extra work for others.
long_explanation: Workslop refers to AI outputs that appear finished and competent on the surface but are decontextualized, incomplete, or unhelpful, forcing colleagues down the workflow to spend time fixing, completing, or interpreting them. It matters for marketers because it directly damages brand trust when off-brand or context-poor AI content reaches consumers, quietly lowers real campaign ROI behind a surface appearance of productivity, and drains team creative capacity as people correct AI mistakes instead of producing original work. The fix is clear AI usage standards, prompt governance, and quality metrics.
usage_context: A study by researchers at BetterUp Labs and Stanford Social Media Lab, first widely reported by Harvard Business Review, finding that 40% of 1,150 surveyed employees encountered workslop in just the past month, and that 95% of companies report no tangible return on their AI investments.
related_terms: prompt governance, AI culture, quality metrics, worksmart, ROI
tr_equivalent: Workslop (Türkçe blogda İngilizce terim aynen kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Görünüşte kaliteli ama gerçekte eksik, alakasız ya da değer katmayan, başkalarına ek iş yükü yaratan yapay zeka çıktılarıdır.

short_definition: Using AI to measure and predict the depth of a consumer's ongoing emotional and behavioral connection to a brand, beyond repeat purchases.
long_explanation: Brand Stickiness Modeling analyzes behavioral data (visit frequency, dwell time, engagement), sentiment (social media and review tone), and engagement patterns across channels to model how strongly and durably a consumer stays connected to a brand. It matters for marketers because, unlike traditional loyalty programs that reward past transactions, stickiness models are predictive: they forecast future brand affinity and let brands adapt content and timing in real time to deepen emotional connection rather than just tracking points or purchases.
usage_context: The concept is attributed to Jacqueline Woods, CMO of Teradata, introduced on Episode 25 of the Decoding AI for Marketers podcast, quoting her: "We help companies create deeper and more engaging experiences so they can become more sticky."
related_terms: loyalty programs, sentiment analysis, predictive modeling, behavioral psychology, Decoding AI for Marketers podcast, Teradata
tr_equivalent: Marka Yapışkanlığı Modellemesi (blogda çoğunlukla İngilizce "Brand Stickiness Modeling" olarak kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Yapay zeka kullanarak bir tüketicinin bir markayla kurduğu sürekli duygusal ve davranışsal bağın derinliğini ölçme ve öngörme yöntemidir.

short_definition: A future-focused alternative to feedback that offers constructive suggestions for what to do better next time instead of critiquing what already happened.
long_explanation: Feedforward replaces backward-looking evaluation (feedback) with forward-looking, solution-oriented guidance, for example saying "next time, keep your message shorter" instead of "your presentation was too long." It matters for marketing and leadership because it increases motivation and creativity in teams, shifts customer communication and campaign analysis from blame to improvement, and makes brands appear more innovative and trustworthy. The mindset connects directly to MMA Global's Project ROMI, which also focuses on forecasting the future business impact of marketing investment rather than only reporting past results.
usage_context: Illustrative examples: reframing "this ad underperformed" as "in the next campaign, targeting Segment X can boost conversions," and reframing a past delivery problem as a promise of faster shipping next time.
related_terms: Project ROMI, CMO/CFO Alignment, MMA Global, leadership communication
tr_equivalent: Feedforward (Türkçe blogda İngilizce terim aynen kullanılmış)
tr_definition: Geçmişi eleştirmek yerine gelecekte daha iyi performans için yapıcı ve çözüm odaklı öneriler sunan bir yaklaşımdır.
